# Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**Member:** Taylor Kimura
**Member ID:** W354999576
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Kansas
**Denial date:** 2026-07-31
**Reference number:** POC-37F3AA304D-16940
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (effective 2026-08-04), https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), which my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented is needed. The denial notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision, because when I look at the records already on file alongside your own published policy, I believe they show what the policy requires.

## How my records match the plan's own criteria

Cigna's policy states that "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The policy then lists, among the required elements:

> "◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

My records show the following:

- **Groin-dominant pain and impingement-type symptoms:** My clinical exam documents "positive provocative testing on the affected side" and range of motion "limited by pain." I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and I cannot run or squat.
- **Failure of non-surgical management lasting at least three months:** I completed 16 weeks (24 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, from 2026-02-23 to 2026-06-15, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also tried NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging findings consistent with FAI:** My MRI arthrogram from 2026-06-24 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees, joint space preserved, and Tonnis grade 0.

I am not able to confirm from the citation I was given exactly which radiographic findings the plan lists under its FAI non-indications section, since that excerpt was cut off before naming them. I would ask Cigna to identify specifically, in writing, which radiographic finding in my imaging it believes falls under that exclusion, if that is the basis for the denial, so that my surgeon and I can respond to it directly.

## Request

I am requesting that Cigna reconsider this denial and approve the requested hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) based on the medical necessity criteria above and the records already in my file. If any specific document or piece of information is still considered missing, please tell me exactly what is needed so my surgeon's office can provide it.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-27. I am submitting it by logging in at my.cigna.com to locate my plan's appeal form, and/or by calling the number on my member ID card (1-800-244-6224). I understand the mailing address for appeals is the one printed on my denial letter, and I will use that address if submitting by mail.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

[Patient signature]
Taylor Kimura
Member ID: W354999576
[Contact phone number]
[Contact email address]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
